metaData.originalTitle: 从 Prompt、Context 到 Harness，工程的三次进化与终局之战
metaData.title: From Prompt to Context to Harness: The Three Evolutions of Engineering and the Endgame
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically elaborates on the three evolutions of AI engineering—from Prompt Engineering to Context Engineering to Harness Engineering—emphasizing that they are nested rather than substitutive, and introduces the Harness Decay Law and a new paradigm for engineers.
metaData.summary: Using the example of a 3-7 person team at OpenAI generating nearly 1 million lines of production-grade code with AI in 5 months, the article systematically outlines the three evolutions of AI engineering. The first evolution, Prompt Engineering, addresses the issue of 'saying it clearly,' but its marginal benefits diminish as model comprehension improves. The second evolution, Context Engineering, tackles the problem of 'providing sufficient information,' encompassing key techniques such as RAG, context compression, and a single source of truth. The third evolution, Harness Engineering, solves the challenge of 'system reliability,' leveraging strategies like context governance, validation loops, and technical debt cleanup to manage AI. The article emphasizes that these three are nested layers, and introduces the Harness Decay Law—the more capable the model, the simpler the required Harness. Finally, it posits that the new paradigm for engineers is 'Human Steer, Agents Execute,' shifting their core responsibility from writing code to setting direction, building frameworks, and making judgments.
metaData.featuredReason: This article details the three evolutions of AI engineering: Prompt, Context, and Harness Engineering. It reveals how OpenAI's team leveraged Harness Engineering to generate nearly a million lines of production code, highlighting the paradigm shift for engineers from coding to designing reliable AI systems. This offers critical insights for adapting to the AI era.

mainPoints.point: AI engineering has undergone three evolutions—Prompt, Context, and Harness—which are nested rather than substitutive.
mainPoints.explanation: Prompt addresses what to say, Context addresses what to know, and Harness addresses how to operate reliably. Without a good Prompt, Context information cannot be correctly understood; without good Context, the Agent operates blindly in an information vacuum; without a good Harness, the Agent accumulates errors and eventually collapses in complex tasks.

mainPoints.point: Harness Engineering is currently a necessary condition for reliable AI system operation, but it is subject to the Decay Law.
mainPoints.explanation: The more capable the model, the simpler the required Harness. As models evolve, many of today's meticulously designed Harness rules will be naturally absorbed by future model capabilities. Engineers should dynamically adjust Harness thickness and avoid over-engineering.

mainPoints.point: The new paradigm for engineers is 'Human Steer, Agents Execute,' with core responsibilities shifting from writing code to designing systems.
mainPoints.explanation: An engineer's value is reflected in the Harness system they build, with core responsibilities shifting to setting direction, building frameworks, and making judgments. Metrics shift from individual code output to system leverage.

keyQuotes: Don't over-engineer solutions for problems that models will naturally solve in the future.
Software engineering hasn't disappeared; it's evolving. From 'someone who writes code' to 'someone who designs systems that let AI write code well.'

Prompt Engineering answers: 'What should I say to the model?' Context Engineering answers: 'What should the model know when answering?' Harness Engineering answers: 'How should the entire AI system operate reliably?'

relatedArticles.title: Investing 10,000 RMB in AI: A Year of Tools, Practices, and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: How I Spent a Week Boosting AI Coding Rate to 90% in an Enterprise App
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces Harness Engineering, a new AI coding paradigm that elevates the AI code rate of an enterprise Java application from 25% to over 90% by building a four-element system of rules, skills, knowledge, and change management.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: GPT-5.4 Released: OpenAI's First Unified Model, Truly Native
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI releases GPT-5.4, creating the first unified Agent model that supports native Computer Use by integrating reasoning, coding, and computer interaction.

relatedArticles.title: 5 Lessons Learned from 400 Million Tokens: What Happened When 6 AI Agents Wrote Code for 4 Days Straight?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Through a four-day multi-agent automated programming experiment, this article reveals that 'glue code' and engineering stability are more challenging and critical than prompt design when building AI systems.

relatedArticles.title: Thinking About Agentic Engineering from First Principles
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically derives six core best practices for Agentic Engineering from first principles and introduces a modular, Skill-based open-source framework, aiming to combine engineering discipline with AI capabilities to reliably improve software engineering quality under complex constraints.

relatedArticles.title: RAG is Dead? No, Grep is Back!
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the leaked source code of Claude Code, this article deeply deconstructs its abandonment of RAG and vector retrieval in favor of an LLM-driven multi-round iterative Grep search mechanism. It compares this approach with Cursor and Codex, demonstrating the feasibility and design philosophy of a zero-index solution in code search scenarios.

relatedArticles.title: What You Don't Know About Claude Code: Architecture, Governance, and Engineering Practices - Tw93
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of Claude Code's six-layer architecture and engineering practices, proposing a systematic Agent development methodology from context governance and skill design to a verification loop.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Hermes in One Article: How the New Top-Tier Agent Self-Evolves from Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core innovation of the Hermes Agent—the Skills closed-loop system—detailing its complete implementation mechanism, from experience extraction and knowledge storage to intelligent retrieval and self-improvement, along with its engineering trade-offs and security considerations.

relatedArticles.title: E45 Meng Yan in Conversation with Li Jigang: How Humans Find Their Place
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This episode explores the inevitable transition from mental labor to 'heart power' in the AI era, and the deep philosophy of responding to technological change by reconstructing investment, education, and mental models.
